summary: Quagnoth adds an unprinted graveyard restriction to the discarded-card return.
status: New; needs upstream review. Still counted as different by the grammar scorer.

cards.name: Quagnoth
cards.text:
Split second
Shroud
When a spell or ability an opponent controls causes you to discard this card, return it to your hand.

reason: The card returns itself after an opponent causes its discard without requiring it to be in the graveyard. A replacement can send the discarded card to exile while the discard trigger still occurs; the reference InZone(Graveyard) query then selects nothing. The native Discarded reference explicitly tracks the card after a discard wherever replacements sent it.
regression_scenarios: Ordinary discard into the graveyard returns the card.
An opponent-caused discard modified to put the card in exile still permits the return from that first public destination.
Tergrid explicitly requires a graveyard card and must retain its graveyard restriction.
evidence: Pinned Comprehensive Rules effective 2026-09-25, saved as reports/local/ir-grammar/work/event-destination-repair/rules.txt.
Frozen native IR documentation: rust_syntax/ir/src/ir.rs ObjectRef::Discarded versus EventDestination.
Saved current-reference gold and every grammar reading in work/event-destination-repair/before.jsonl and after.jsonl.
source_fix_note: Check the source/template classification of Quagnoth’s returned-card operand before regenerating the reference. Do not globally remove explicit graveyard guards from other cards.
producer: English template returns the discarded event object rather than a graveyard-specific reference.

validation.bindings: New tagged Action member verified against ts-rs output; unrelated pre-existing bundled binding drift preserved
